text:
mia: Heads-up — customer on org 'acme-inc' says project 'acme-web' shows 0 remaining in the quota tile but they're not getting 429s until later in the day. Dashboard vs API mismatch. anyone seen this pattern?

samir: Noted. Do we have a repro request from the customer (timestamps + sample request IDs)?

mia: Yes — sent sample request ids in support ticket. Customer says dashboard flipped to 0 at 09:12 UTC but API returned 200 for ~800 requests until 09:45 then a burst of 429s.

olivia: Could be rolling-window alignment vs ledger ingestion lag. Dashboard uses a windowed aggregate with a 1m rollup TTL, ingestion can be delayed if uplink backlog.

billing-bot: FYI: recent ingestion backfill job had a 3-6m lag between 08:50-09:50 UTC (job id job-ingest-20260309-2).

jordan: That ingest lag could make tiles show an artificially low remaining quota (tile counts are conservative snapshots). But we should confirm whether org-level shared pool is being double-counted in the tile.

ashlee: Quick check I did: project shows limit 100k/min, org pool 500k/min. At 09:12 dashboard showed project remaining 0 but org remaining ~120k. So UI might be prioritizing project enforcement view but counting org usage in a separate aggregation.

samir: Can we get the exact SQL we use for the tile so support can explain to customer? I'll paste a query to run in metering DB.

samir: ```
-- approximate example, run in metering-read replica
SELECT sum(tokens) as tokens_used,
       time_bucket('60s', ts) as bucket
FROM usage.tokens
WHERE project_id = 'acme-web' AND ts >= '2026-03-09T09:00:00Z' AND ts < '2026-03-09T10:00:00Z'
GROUP BY bucket
ORDER BY bucket;
```

mia: I ran that against their sample IDs — shows steady usage until 09:44 then a 429 burst window. Matches customer logs. However UI tile hit 0 at 09:12.

olivia: Two hypotheses: 1) dashboard UI precomputes expected rolling-window consumption using a cached shard summary that got stale during ingestion lag; 2) project-level quota enforcement is using a different rolling-window alignment (tenant-local timezone vs UTC) causing an offset.

ashlee: Also check if request routing fell back to another region (and counted against org pool instead) then later got re-sharded back — that could produce transient mismatch in project tiles.

samir: For quick repro steps for infra: 1) replay customer sample with same RPS into our staging metering; 2) tail ingester logs for job-ingest-*; 3) run the sum(tokens) by bucket and compare with tile snapshot stored in redis (key pattern: quota:tiles:project:{project_id}:window:{window_start}).

jordan: Note for support response: be explicit about possible delays — explain that dashboard tiles are eventually consistent and can temporally appear to show 0 while API still allows requests until ledger ingestion triggers enforcement. Suggest mitigation: enable org-level reserve or set project burst cushion.

mia: I'll draft a support reply listing the repro steps + the backfill job note. Any wording suggestions?

olivia: Short and concrete: "We investigated — tile shows 0 due to a metric ingestion lag and rolling-window alignment between project vs org aggregates. Enforcement is based on ledger state and can lag the UI; we saw an ingestion backlog around 09:00-09:50 which caused the tile to appear low earlier than enforcement. We're recommending a temporary org cushion and we've queued a backfill to reconcile tiles." Add the job id and ETA.

mia: Perfect. I'll send that and include the SQL + snippet for them to paste if they want to verify. Thanks all :thumbsup:

billing-bot: Note: backfill job job-ingest-20260309-2 completed at 09:58 UTC and reconciliation ran — delta was ~+21k tokens for acme-web for the 09:00-09:50 window.
